title: MyVector — cross-engine vector search
subtitle: MyVector · vsql_vector · pgvector · MariaDB — fashion-mnist-784, full metrics
nav: ★ fair same-host (optimized) · MySQL versions (8.4/9.7/26.10) · real-dataset by version · village (recall/QPS) · 8.4 family · 9.7 family
description: MyVector's native HNSW vector search for MySQL, head-to-head with VillageSQL's vsql_vector, pgvector, and MariaDB's native vector index on a real dataset (fashion-mnist-784-euclidean, 60k × 784, L2) with the dataset's published ground truth and full metrics (build, insert, exact-KNN, ANN p50/p99, recall@10). This is the 9.7-base cross-engine view; see the 8.4 / 9.7 family pages for per-base detail, MySQL versions for MyVector across 8.4/9.7/26.10, and village for the same four engines through VillageSQL's neutral vector-dev-bench harness.
caveats: Full metrics via MyVector's harness: index build, insert QPS, exact brute-force KNN (QPS + p50/p99), ANN (QPS + p50/p99), and recall@10 vs the dataset's published ground truth. Headline cards are the warm ef_search=200 point.

Dataset: fashion-mnist-784-euclidean (60k train × 784-d, 10k test, L2). HNSW M=16, ef_construction=200 for MyVector/vsql_vector/pgvector; MariaDB's MHNSW fixes ef_construction at 10 internally. MariaDB also floors mhnsw_ef_search to ~2×M (≈32), so an ef_search=10 request is not a valid operating point for it — that point is omitted from MariaDB's plotted curve (its measured value is kept in the result JSON under ef_search_excluded for transparency). Every other engine applies no such floor, so their ef_search=10 points are plotted as-is.
Engines here are on the 9.7 base (MyVector on MySQL 9.7, vsql_vector on the VillageSQL 9.7 dev-server) plus pgvector (Postgres 17) and MariaDB 12.3. The 8.4 family is the 8.4-base companion.
Cache parity: each engine's graph sized above the ~188 MB index. Hardware: all on the same Ampere A1 dev host.
A bigger cosine dataset (glove-100-angular, 1.2M) is benchmarking separately and will get its own page.
